new_candidates.body:
(Per discussion in PR #25102)

### Background
Standard SDFormat provides a set of joints defined by the `<joint>` tag which contains tags `<parent>` and `<child>`. Drake has additional joints defined by the `<drake:joint>` tag which contains tags `<drake:parent>` and `<drake:child>`. The sematics of `<drake:parent>` and standard `<parent>` are subtly different (also for `<child>`). They probably should not be different.

The difference is as follows. `<drake:parent>` implements Drake joint semantics directly. It defines both (a) the parent link, and (b) the parent frame Jp on that link. Similarly `<drake:child>` defines the child link and frame Jc on that link. In contrast, standard `<parent>` defines the parent link (even if given a frame) but a joint frame J is inferred by various heuristics involving the specified poses of the parent and child links. Then we generate Jp and Jc for Drake assuming they are coincident with J.

PR #25102 extends SDFormat's standard `<joint>` to contain additional tags `<drake:parent_frame>` and `<drake:child_frame>` to explicitly provide Jp and Jc. Those aren't needed in the Drake extension joints since the `<drake:parent>` and child tags perform that extra duty already.

### Proposal
Make the `<drake:parent>` and `<drake:child>` tags have the reduced functionality of the standard tags and then allow `<drake:joint>` to use `<drake:parent_frame>` etc to provide explicit Jp and Jc frames.

### Discussion
The proposed change would be a breaking change if anyone is already specifying frame in a `<drake:joint>`. The workaround would be to add the new tags. Although the `<drake:joint>` behavior is the correct one, we would gain consistency by nerfing it.
new_candidates.title: [parsing] Inconsistent semantics between <drake:parent> and standard <parent> in sdf
